verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing is on by default. After a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 or more pages, the connection that committed runs a checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages' ... 'run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP. A NOOP checkpoint always checkpoints zero frames
verdicts.evidence: changes.html 2025-11-04 (3.51.0): 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'; c3ref: 'This mode always checkpoints zero frames'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row of three integers ... counts are -1 when the database is not in WAL mode, and both are 0 after a successful TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'single row with three integer columns' / '-1 if there is no write-ahead log'; c3ref: 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero' after TRUNCATE

verdicts.claim: The WAL-Reset bug is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). The fix shipped in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and 3.53.0 (2026-04-09), with backports 3.50.7 and 3.44.6; 3.52.0 withdrawn; newest 3.54.0
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)' / 'fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later', backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7; changes.html: 3.52.0 'Withdrawn', 3.53.0 2026-04-09, 3.54.0 2026-10-09. Reason for withdrawal (stale expression index) not checked.

verdicts.claim: Tailscale's control plane ... hit the WAL-Reset bug in 19 separate database corruptions over six months starting in August 2025
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months'; first incident 'August last year' in a 2026-08-12 post

verdicts.claim: Tailscale's metrics showed SQLite reporting more pages copied from the WAL than the WAL contained (for example 20 pages copied from a 10-page WAL)
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: metrics showed SQLite 'copying more pages from the WAL file than were actually available', example 10 pages in WAL, 20 copied

verdicts.claim: Antithesis reproduced the WAL-Reset bug in SQLite 3.51.2 on its first run, within 15 minutes ... the same test on 3.51.3 passed
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; on 3.51.3 'the run came back green'; workload 'just runs writes and checkpoints concurrently'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5 ... recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0 plus PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 ... truncate-page-n (default 121359 pages, about 500 MB) PASSIVE first (since v0.5.15)
verdicts.evidence: tips: read lock between checkpoint requests, 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000', 'PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0'; guide: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', min-checkpoint-page-count 1000, checkpoint-interval 1m, PASSIVE tried first before forced TRUNCATE

verdicts.claim: Android defaults db_wal_autocheckpoint to 100 pages ... db_wal_truncate_size (default 1048576) ... Android also defaults db_wal_sync_mode to NORMAL
Firefox Places sets PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint to DATABASE_MAX_WAL_BYTES (2048000) divided by the page size, and sets journal_size_limit to 2048000 + 2048000
verdicts.evidence: Database.cpp: '#define DATABASE_MAX_WAL_BYTES 2048000', checkpointPages = DATABASE_MAX_WAL_BYTES / aDBPageSize; journal_size_limit = DATABASE_MAX_WAL_BYTES + DATABASE_JOURNAL_OVERHEAD_BYTES (2048000)
